references.text: Abraham makes his servant swear by the Lord, the God of heaven, just as Rahab asks the spies to swear by the Lord.
Abimelek asks Abraham to swear that he will show kindness (chesed) to him, just as Rahab asks for kindness in return for the kindness she has shown.
Jacob asks Joseph to show him faithful love (chesed ve'emet), using the same wording as Rahab when she requests a reliable sign.
The fulfillment of the promise given to Rahab - the spies keep the oath they swore, and Rahab's family is spared.
A similar promise of kindness is given to a man who helps the Israelites, parallel to Rahab's situation.
Jonathan asks David to show the Lord's faithfulness (chesed) toward him and his house, the same kind of covenant for mutual protection.
David shows kindness (chesed) toward Jonathan's house, as an example of keeping an oath of mutual protection.
Rahab is mentioned as an example of faith - she received the spies in peace, which led to her being spared.
Rahab is highlighted as justified by works when she received the messengers and sent them out by another way.
